answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by locking each new identity's bond for twice as long as the last one sharing its funding source: the first fake's stake is frozen one epoch, the tenth for hundreds, the thousandth for longer than the ledger has lived. A falcon-eyed protocol reads the funding trail on-chain, not the operator's word, and no ledge of spare capital lets a farm climb past the clock — each extra head traps its own bond under basalt-hard time, so bulk farming strands its money instead of multiplying it.
